Dataloy Distance API Integration
Connect Dataloy VMS to enable live port name lookup and validated sailing distances · API key is stored locally in browser only
Not Connected
Dataloy API Key
Blank = uses the shared server-side default key automatically. Anything you type here is stored in browser localStorage only — never transmitted to any third party — and overrides the shared key just for this browser.
API Endpoint URL
Defaults to this site's own /api/dataloy-proxy — that's what supplies the shared key and fixes CORS. Calling Dataloy directly from the browser is always CORS-blocked, so a proxy is required either way.
Route Mode
Auto uses Dataloy routing intelligence — recommended
ℹ Ready — enter API key and click Test Connection
Port Distance Lookup — Test Query
Query the Dataloy Distance API directly to verify port names and distances before use in voyage legs.
Distance result will appear here after query.
Live Port Lookup
Dynamic port search from Dataloy VMS database with 5,000+ global ports. Replaces local dropdown list when API is active.
Validated Distances
Dataloy routing engine provides ETA-validated sailing distances via optimal commercial sea routes including canal transits.
Offline Fallback
Built-in 180+ port haversine engine with canal correction table remains active as fallback when API is unavailable.
Secure Transmission
API key stored locally in browser. All requests are HTTPS. No voyage data or API keys leave your browser to any third-party server.
UN/LOCODE Support
Ports identified by UN/LOCODE standard codes (e.g. SGSIN, JPCHB) for unambiguous port identification in all voyage records.
Get API Access
Requires active Dataloy VMS subscription. Contact dataloy.com for Chemical Tanker API access.

Load rotation

Reads the Ports Rotation column of the Ship Ops Tracker.

Reads the Ports Rotation column of B · Port Rotation, Bunker, Sail-Port Days in the Ship Voy calculator.

The Ship Ops report keeps every field in an embedded data block, so the rotation, dates and port days come across exactly.

Port rotation

    Stay in hours alongside. Click a port on the chart to add it.

    Route options

    Load a rotation or pick two ports, then Find routes.

    Tick plans to compare them on the chart. Plans are kept in this browser. Click the title Saved Plans for the table. Upload RTZ on a plan, then Load, draws that RTZ (dashed) over the saved plan.

    Find vessel

      Search a vessel to draw its AIS track from A to B.

      Import AIS track

      CSV needs lat and lon, and ideally timestamp, mmsi, sog and cog. NMEA message types 1, 2, 3, 5 and 18.

      Live track

      Send a plan

      Inbox

      Sent

      Exchange contract 
      POST {endpoint}/outbox      { planName, to, channel, note, rtzVersion, fileName, rtz }
                            → 202 { id }
GET  {endpoint}/inbox       → [{ id, from, note, fileName, rtz, receivedAt }]
GET  {endpoint}/vessels/{mmsi}/track?hours=72
                            → [{ t, lat, lon, sog, cog }]
Dataloy proxy:  {proxy}/route/route?point=[lat,lon]&point=…&block_sc=true
                {proxy}/port/port?filter=portName(EQ)SINGAPORE

      Set the endpoints under Settings › AIS Map. Keys stay on your server; the Dataloy key can also sit in this browser for direct calls, like the AI key.

      Settings
      Look · Comfort · AIS Map · AI · Local LLM · Files

      Theme

      How the app looks and feels. Day / Night stays on the moon button in the top bar.

      Look
      Calm: navy and cyan. Focus: graphite, one muted accent. Playful: rounder, warm pink accent.

      Comfort

      Settings are saved in this browser.

      Motion
      Reduced switches off animations and transitions.
      Contrast
      High contrast brightens text and borders.
      Hover tooltips
      Off hides the explainer bubbles that appear on hover.
      Font size
      Scales the whole layout together so tables and cards still fit. Medium is the default.
      Colors
      Accent palette for buttons, highlights and charts. Works with Day / Night and every look.

      AIS Map

      Chart look, layers and data connections for the AIS Map tab. Saved in this browser.

      Chart theme
      Day, Dusk and Night follow the ECDIS palettes. Follow app switches with the moon button.
      Grid

      Local LLM model

      Detects models served on this computer (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, Jan, vLLM) and re-scans automatically, so a model appears soon after you start Ollama. Nothing leaves your machine.

      Press Detect to scan
      Setup guide: let this page connect to Ollama (OLLAMA_ORIGINS)

      Browsers only let a page talk to Ollama if Ollama allows the page's origin. A page opened as a file on your computer has the origin "null", which Ollama blocks by default. That is why Detect can show "No local models found" even though Ollama is running. Setting OLLAMA_ORIGINS=* fixes it.

      Windows (Ollama in the system tray)

      1. Right-click the Ollama icon in the system tray and choose Quit.
      2. Open PowerShell and run: setx OLLAMA_ORIGINS "*"
        (Or: Start menu → "Edit environment variables for your account" → New → Name OLLAMA_ORIGINS, Value *.)
      3. Start Ollama again from the Start menu. Open a new window first: a window opened before this will not see the new setting.

      macOS

      1. Quit the Ollama app from the menu bar.
      2. In Terminal run: launchctl setenv OLLAMA_ORIGINS "*"
      3. Open the Ollama app again.

      Linux (systemd)

      1. Run sudo systemctl edit ollama and add under [Service]: Environment="OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*"
      2. Run sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart ollama

      Quick test from a terminal (any system): OLLAMA_ORIGINS=* ollama serve (PowerShell: $env:OLLAMA_ORIGINS="*"; ollama serve)

      Check it worked

      • Open http://localhost:11434 in a browser: it should say "Ollama is running".
      • Run ollama list. If it is empty, pull a model first, for example ollama pull llama3.2.
      • Come back here. This page re-scans every few seconds, so the model appears without pressing Detect. Then select it, press Test, then Use this model.

      Note: * lets any web page you open call your local Ollama. If that worries you, serve this file from http://localhost instead (Ollama already allows localhost pages), or quit Ollama when you are not using it.
